title: Priority fanout routing with soft-quota degradation and model-variant fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a priority-aware fanout router that prefers higher-paying tiers (enterprise > paid > free), respects per-tenant and per-key quotas, and degrades requests gracefully using model-variant fallbacks instead of hard rejections. This ticket covers routing policy, quota accounting hooks, and fallback strategy for availability and cost control.

Scope: router decision logic, quota check adapter, soft-degradation modes (reduction in concurrency, model swap to cheaper variant, response shortening), and telemetry hooks for cost/latency attribution. Does NOT include UI changes to the Console (separate PM ticket).
updates: 2025-02-12: Initial spec authored; documented desired behaviors for free/paid/enterprise priorities and soft-degradation modes.

2025-02-15: Spike completed: microbenchmark shows model-variant swap adds ~12-18ms median for small requests but reduces token spend by ~45% on average for large generations. Results in /docs/spikes/model_variant_swap_2025-02-15.md (linked).

2025-02-18: Design review with PM and runtime leads. Agreed on three soft-fallback tiers: (1) same-model quantized variant, (2) smaller architecture (e.g., 7B vs 13B), (3) constrained-response policy (max tokens + prefix caching).

2025-02-22: Implemented quota adapter interface and unit tests. Adapter exposes check(), reserve(), commit()/revert() hooks. Integration tests pending. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/ENG-15678-priority-fanout (WIP).

2025-02-25: Canary routing configured in eu-west-1 for 5 internal tenants. Observability dashboards: routing-priority-2025-02 (links below). Initial canary traffic shows correct preference ordering but some tenants observe increased 429s due to quota race — added optimistic reservation to mitigate.
2025-02-28: Switched optimistic reservation to a 100ms transient hold; 429s reduced by ~72%. Preparing for broader canary and postmortem notes for race condition handling.
acceptance_criteria: Router selects highest available tier (enterprise > paid > free) for a request when quota allows and respects region affinity policy.
When quota insufficient, router attempts soft-degradation strategies in configured priority order before returning an error.
Quota adapter exposes atomic reserve/commit/revert semantics to prevent double-allocations under concurrent fanout.
Telemetry emitted for every routing decision: chosen tier, fallback used, tokens billed, latency, and quota outcome.
End-to-end integration tests that simulate concurrent requests across tiers and assert no more than X% unexpected 429s (X=1% for enterprise, 5% for paid, 10% for free) under target load.
technical_notes: Decision: implement soft-degradation in router layer rather than in model-serving to keep fallbacks consistent across Dedicated/Private/Hosted deployments.
Quota model: token-based sliding-window with a short-duration optimistic reservation (default 100ms) to reduce races between parallel fanouts. Reservation granularity configurable per-plan.

Fallback policy order: 1) quantized same-architecture variant (low perf delta), 2) smaller model variant with shorter max tokens, 3) cached prefix response + requester notification, 4) hard reject with 429.
Routing score = weighted_sum(priority_score, remaining_quota_ratio, region_latency_penalty, cost_multiplier). Weights are config-driven and stored in config service with rollout flags.

Model compatibility matrix maintained in model-catalog; router consults catalog to ensure fallback variant preserves API/structured-output compatibility or triggers structured-output-safe fallback (e.g., run in a validation step).
Trade-off: model-variant swaps can affect output quality. To mitigate, run lightweight evals on recent prompts and surface quality regression alerts in console for canaries.
risks: Quality regression for latency-driven fallbacks — could impact user-facing applications. Mitigation: automatic quality monitors, rollback runbooks.
Quota race windows causing transient double-counting or excess rejections. Mitigation: optimistic reservations + reconcile job that corrects counters asynchronously.

Cross-region consistency: user pinned to a region might be routed to fallback region for capacity; must respect data residency and VPC policies. Mitigation: region-aware constraints enforced before applying fallbacks.
Increased complexity in billing attribution when model variants differ in cost — need per-variant cost_factor and downstream billing adjustments.
open_questions: Should fallback order be configurable per-tenant via Console? (PM: prefer opt-in for enterprise customers only due to potential quality impact).
What is safe default reservation window for high concurrency tenants? Current spike shows 100ms works for small canary; may need adaptive window per QPS.
Do we allow cross-tier borrowing (e.g., paid request temporarily use enterprise capacity) when paid is exhausted but enterprise has spare capacity? (Security and billing implications).
